title: AppManifest
description: The app manifest (`pithyx.json` at the root of an app package), version 2 (D388). It tells the daemon and the desktop what the app is, what it may do and why, and how its window and backend behave. The icon is always `icon.svg` next to it. This schema is a stable contract: a new optional field is a minor change, anything else a major one. Unknown fields are errors.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, for editors. Ignored by the box.

manifestVersion.description: The manifest schema this file follows. A box refuses a manifest of another version with `app.manifest.version_unsupported`; version 1 ended with Pithyx 1.2 (D388).

version.description: SemVer 2.0 version of the app, without build metadata, for example `1.2.0` or `2.0.0-beta.1`.

license.description: SPDX license expression of the app, for example `MIT` or `MIT OR Apache-2.0`.

homepage.description: The app's website or source repository.

source.description: Where the app's source code is: the URL of its repository, or `private` when the source is not public. The Store shows "Open source" for a public source with a `license`, and "Source not public" otherwise.

privacy.description: What the app sends out of the box, shown openly in the Store (D389): `none` (nothing), `optional` (only what a user switches on, such as a link to an account), `telemetry` (usage or crash data to its author) or `vendorAccount` (it needs an account at a service outside the box). `note` says more in the author's words. Catalogs require it.

sends.description: What the app sends out of the box.

security.description: Where to report a vulnerability of the app: an `https` URL or a `mailto:` address. The Store shows it on the app's page; `pithyx validate` recommends it for apps with high or critical rights.

maturity.description: How far the app is: `stable`, `beta` or `experimental`. The Store shows `beta` and `experimental` as a badge. Without it the app counts as `stable`.

categories.description: Up to three categories from a fixed list, for the Store's filter.

keywords.description: Up to 10 words the Store's search finds the app by, besides its name and description, in any language. Each 1 to 30 characters on one line.

locales.description: The languages the app's own interface is in, as BCP 47 tags such as `en` or `pt-BR`. The Store says which of them match the user's language.

screenshots.description: Up to 8 pictures of the app for its Store page: files in the package under `frontend/` (PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 1 MiB each), each with an optional caption. An installed app serves them with its frontend.

requirements.description: What the app needs to run well, as a hint: the install dialog warns when the box or the app pool has less, and installs anyway.

memory.description: About how much memory the app uses while it runs, in MB.

disk.description: About how much space the app's data takes on the app pool, in MB.

audience.description: Who the app is for: `everyone` or `admins`. It is the default of "Who may use it" when the app is installed; an app that may see every user, runs as root or asks for special rights is still suggested for administrators. The administrator can change it.

entry.description: Path of the HTML page the desktop loads in the sandboxed window, inside `frontend/` of the package, for example `frontend/index.html`. Segments never start with a dot.

sdk.description: SemVer range of `@pithyx/sdk` the app was built against, for example `^1.0.0`.

pithyx.description: SemVer range of the Pithyx versions the app runs on, for example `>=0.1.0`. Optional; without it the app claims to run on every version. A box installs a version only when its own version is in the range, and lists a catalog version only then. Unlike npm, a box running a prerelease matches by plain SemVer precedence, so `>=0.1.0` includes `0.2.0-beta.1`, while `^0.1.0` does not (it ends below `0.2.0-0`). Catalogs require it.

dataVersion.description: The version of the format of the app's stored data (volumes, its stored values and the files of its storage requests), an integer from 1. Optional. Raise it with every release that converts data in a way the previous version cannot read. A box goes back to an older version from a catalog only when both declare the same `dataVersion`; going back to the version before an update with its snapshot works without it.

arch.description: The processor architectures the app runs on: `amd64` (x86-64) and `arm64`. Every image of the backend must exist for each of them. A box refuses to install the app on another architecture (`app.arch.unsupported`), because it cannot run there; an app without a backend usually names both.

storage.description: Places for files the app needs, each mapped by an administrator to a folder in a shared folder.

fileActions.description: Actions the app adds to the context menu of files and folders, for example "Extract here" on archives. Needs the permission `files.shares`.

notifications.description: How the app's notifications are sorted (D390). Needs the permission `notifications`.

categories.description: Up to 16 kinds of notifications the app sends, such as new messages or reminders. Each user can mute a kind in the notification settings; `notify` names the kind with `category`.

VersionRange.description: A SemVer range in the npm range syntax without the loose forms: comparators (`^`, `~`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `=`), `x` and `*` wildcards, hyphen ranges with spaces around the dash, sets joined by ` || `.

AppId.title: AppId
AppId.description: The author's domain reversed plus the app name: 3 to 5 parts of lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at most 100 characters, for example `com.mueller.chat` or `io.github.jan.chat`. Unique per box. `org.pithyx.*` is reserved for the system apps and the official catalog.

LocalizedName.title: LocalizedName
LocalizedName.description: A short text in several languages, keyed by BCP 47 language tag, for example the app's name or a storage request's name. `en` is required and used when nothing else matches. One line, at most 60 characters per language.

en.description: The English text, shown when no other language matches. One line, at most 60 characters.

^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8})*$.description: The text in the language of the key, a BCP 47 language tag such as `de` or `pt-BR`. One line, at most 60 characters.

LocalizedText.title: LocalizedText
LocalizedText.description: A text in several languages, keyed by BCP 47 language tag, for example the app's description of one or two sentences for the store and the install dialog. `en` is required and used when nothing else matches. At most 500 characters per language; line breaks are allowed.

en.description: The English text, shown when no other language matches. At most 500 characters; line breaks are allowed.

^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8})*$.description: The text in the language of the key, a BCP 47 language tag such as `de` or `pt-BR`. At most 500 characters; line breaks are allowed.

HttpUrl.description: An `http` or `https` URL of printable ASCII characters, at most 500 characters.

Permission.title: Permission
Permission.description: The name of a permission an app declares in `permissions`. Nothing is granted by using an API: the install dialog lists every declared permission, an administrator confirms them for the app, and each one can be revoked later (the app gets `permissionsChange`). Which users may use the app at all is a separate grant per user and group. The daemon checks every permission on every call that reaches data or leaves the window. An update that declares a new permission waits until an administrator confirms it; the old version keeps running. `files.read`: read files the user opens with the app or picks in a desktop file dialog. `files.write`: write those files, and save new files where the user chooses in a desktop save dialog. `files.shares`: browse every shared folder the user may access, with the user's own rights. `notifications`: show notifications. `notifications.external`: let them also reach the email and webhook channels of the users, together with `notifications` (D379). `directory.read`: list all users and groups of the box. `network.internet`: outgoing connections to the internet, from the window (`connect-src https:`) and from the backend. `network.lan`: outgoing connections from the backend to the local network (private, shared and link-local addresses such as `192.168.0.0/16`); without it the backend reaches no other device in the LAN, also with `network.internet`. The box itself is never reachable.

ElevatedPermission.title: ElevatedPermission
ElevatedPermission.description: The name of a right beyond the sandbox, for the backend only (D71), declared in `permissions` like the other permissions: `host.network` (the host's network namespace), `host.pid` (the host's process namespace), `device:<path under /dev>` (one device node, for example `device:/dev/net/tun`, or a device class: `device:/dev/dri` for the graphics cards, `device:/dev/serial` for USB serial adapters), `capability:<NAME>` (one Linux capability without the `CAP_` prefix, for example `capability:NET_ADMIN`), `docker.socket` (the Docker Engine API through the daemon's filtering proxy: the app sees and controls only the containers it started), `docker.socket.raw` (the unfiltered Docker Engine API, which is root on the box) and `host.full` (a privileged container: root on the host). The box sorts each into a risk tier (elevated, high or critical, `elevated.tiers` in `compose.v1.rules.json`) that decides how much the install dialog asks; an administrator grants them after a confirmation with password and TOTP (D311, D387, D388), each revocable. Blocked devices and capabilities and `host.full` are refused with `app.elevated.unsupported`. `host.network`, `host.pid` and devices other than `/dev/net/tun` cannot go together with `backend.root` (`app.elevated.root_conflict`), a capability needs it (`app.elevated.root_required`), every one needs a `backend` (`app.elevated.backend_missing`), and `docker.socket` and `docker.socket.raw` exclude each other.

Permissions.title: Permissions
Permissions.description: The permissions and rights the app asks for, by name (`Permission` or `ElevatedPermission`), each with the author's reason (D388). Each one appears with its reason in the install dialog and on the Store page and can be revoked later. `optional` is allowed only on a device right, `hosts` only on `network.internet`; an unknown name is refused.
Permissions.tsType: Record<string, { reason: { en: string; [language: string]: string }; optional?: boolean; hosts?: string[] }>

PlainGrant.title: PlainGrant
PlainGrant.description: A permission or right with its reason.

DeviceGrant.title: DeviceGrant
DeviceGrant.description: A device right with its reason and whether the backend runs without the device.

optional.description: The backend runs without the device, such as a graphics card that only speeds it up (D387). A missing optional device only gives a hint, and the backend starts without it. Every other device is required: without it the app cannot be installed, and its backend does not start until the device is back. Default false.

InternetGrant.title: InternetGrant
InternetGrant.description: `network.internet` with its reason and the hosts the app talks to.

hosts.description: The domains the app talks to, for example `api.example.org`, or `*.example.org` for its subdomains. The Store shows them; the box does not enforce them yet.

Reason.title: Reason
Reason.description: Why the app needs a permission, in the author's words, keyed by BCP 47 language tag, for example "Fetches the weather for your city". `en` is required and used when nothing else matches. One line, at most 200 characters per language. Required for every permission and right (D388).

en.description: The English reason, shown when no other language matches.

^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8})*$.description: The reason in the language of the key, a BCP 47 language tag such as `de` or `pt-BR`.

WindowManifest.title: WindowManifest
WindowManifest.description: How the app's windows behave. `defaultSize` is the size of a new window when the user has no remembered size for the app; `minSize` is the smallest size on screens that can fit it, at most `defaultSize` in both dimensions.

instances.description: `single`: opening the app again focuses the user's existing window on this device and passes the launch arguments to it (`launch` event). `multi`: every launch opens a new window.

suggestAtSignIn.description: Whether the app suggests opening after sign-in, for an app people keep open all day such as a chat. The desktop marks it as suggested where a user chooses the apps that open after signing in; it never opens the app by itself. Default false.

WindowLoading.title: WindowLoading
WindowLoading.description: What a window shows before the app is ready. The desktop always draws the app's icon and name in a new window and an indicator after 300 ms, until the app connected (or, with `untilReady`, until it called `app.window.ready()`). While the backend starts, a line of text says so; without `text` it is the desktop's own, such as "Starting Lists ...". `text` is the line shown while the backend starts, in the user's language, for example "Opening your lists ...": say what happens in plain words, without technical terms.

untilReady.description: Whether the window keeps the placeholder after the app connected until it calls `app.window.ready()`, for an app that first loads its data. The desktop removes it after 30 seconds in any case. Default false.

Name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter, at most 32 characters.

StorageRequest.title: StorageRequest
StorageRequest.description: A place for files the app needs, declared by name and shown to the administrator with its `name`, for example "Photo library". At install an administrator maps it to a folder in a shared folder (and can change that later). The app only ever sees the name and paths inside it: the window reaches it through the SDK file API as `{ storage: id }`, the backend services listed in `services` find it as the Compose volume named `id`. Users reach it with their own rights on the mapped folder, never with more than `access`.

access.description: The most the app may do with the mapped folder: `read` or `readWrite`. Users never get more than their own rights on the folder, and with `read` every backend service mounts it read-only.

required.description: The app cannot start until this storage is mapped.

services.description: Backend services that mount this storage. Needs a `backend`.

FileHandler.title: FileHandler
FileHandler.description: Files the app can open. The desktop offers the app in "Open with" only for these types and sends it only such files (`launch`, `openFile`). An extension belongs to one handler only.

extensions.description: Lowercase extensions without the leading dot, for example `png` or `tar.gz`.

isDefault.description: Whether the app is the default for these files when it is the only handler.

FileAction.title: FileAction
FileAction.description: An entry the desktop adds to the context menu of files and folders in Files, when every selected item matches it. Choosing it opens the app with `launch.action`: the action's `id`, the share, the folder and the names of the selected items, which the app reads and changes through the files API with the user's rights (`files.shares`). `label` is the menu entry, for example "Extract here". Give `extensions`, `folders: true` or both.

id.description: Unique within the app; `launch.action.id` names it.

extensions.description: Files the action applies to: lowercase extensions without the leading dot, for example `zip` or `tar.gz`.

folders.description: Whether the action applies to folders. Default false.

multiple.description: Whether the action takes several selected items at once; otherwise it is offered for exactly one. Default false.

writes.description: Whether the action writes into the folder of the selection, so the desktop offers it only where the user may change files. Default false.

BackendEndpoint.title: BackendEndpoint
BackendEndpoint.description: A port of a backend service that the proxy offers to the app's windows. Container ports never appear in a URL: the endpoint `api` is `/apps/<id>/api/`, every other endpoint `<name>` is `/apps/<id>/api-<name>/`.

port.description: The port the service listens on inside the app's internal network. It never gets a host port.

BackendPath.description: A path on a backend endpoint, starting with `/`.

BackendHealth.title: BackendHealth
BackendHealth.description: The daemon calls `GET path` on `endpoint` to learn whether the backend is ready; a 2xx answer means running.

BackendSchedule.title: BackendSchedule
BackendSchedule.description: A recurring backend job. The daemon starts the backend for it even without an open window and calls `POST path` on `endpoint` when it fires.

id.description: Stable name, unique within the app; the Log Center names it with each run.

cron.description: Five fields separated by single spaces (minute 0-59, hour 0-23, day of month 1-31, month 1-12, day of week 0-7 with 0 and 7 for Sunday), in the box's time zone. Each field is a comma list of `*`, numbers and ranges `a-b`; `*` and ranges may take a step `/n`. No names.

BackendManifest.title: BackendManifest
BackendManifest.description: An optional backend of one or more containers, described by a Compose file in the package and reached only through the daemon's proxy.

compose.description: Path of the Compose file inside `backend/` of the package, usually `backend/compose.yaml`.

endpoints.description: The ports the proxy offers, by name. `api` is required: it is the default endpoint of `app.backend`.

lifecycle.description: `always`: runs while the app is installed and its pool is available. `onDemand`: runs while at least one window of the app is open for any user, plus `idleTimeout`, or while a schedule holds it.

idleTimeout.description: Seconds an `onDemand` backend keeps running after its last window closed. Default 600. Ignored for `always`.

root.description: The containers run as root inside the container (unprivileged on the host through user namespaces). The install dialog warns about it. Default false: they run as the app's own user.

network.description: Which services get the network out of the box that `network.internet` and `network.lan` open. Without it every service gets it; the others stay on the app's internal network only. No effect without one of the two permissions.

services.description: The services of the Compose file that may connect out, for example only the one that fetches.

schedules.description: Recurring jobs that call the backend on a cron schedule, also without an open window.

Screenshot.title: Screenshot
Screenshot.description: A picture of the app in the package.

file.description: The picture's path in the package, under `frontend/`, ending in `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.webp`. The file must exist and be at most 1 MiB.

NotificationCategory.title: NotificationCategory
NotificationCategory.description: One kind of notification the app sends.

id.description: The name `notify` uses for it: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter, at most 32 characters. Unique in the app.
